stories.headline: Meta releases Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its first frontier models

key_facts.fact: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on Monday, October 12, 2026, its first attempt at a frontier model.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta's Superintelligence Lab released a pair of new state-of-the-art models on Monday, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, representing the company's first attempt at a frontier model.

key_facts.fact: Muse Wonder is available via the Meta Model API and Muse Code at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens ($0.20 cached input); Wonder Full is available only to Muse Code subscribers, not through the API.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're excited to launch Muse Wonder on Muse Code and Meta Model API at $4 input / $20 output per million tokens (USD)... Muse Wonder Full, available exclusively by subscription in Muse Code

key_facts.fact: Meta says the models were trained at its gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center and describes Muse Wonder as its most aligned model to date, with a full safety report to come.
key_facts.excerpt: Trained at our gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center... Muse Wonder is our most aligned model to date... A full report with additional safety evaluations will be available soon.

key_facts.fact: Artificial Analysis scored Wonder Full 56 on its Intelligence Index, tying Claude Sonnet 5.5 and ahead of GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Fable 5.1 (53 each); only Claude Opus 5.5 scored higher at 58. Standard Muse Wonder scored 52.
key_facts.excerpt: awarding Wonder Full a score of 56 on its Intelligence Index — tying Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5 and surpassing OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, Google's Gemini 4 Argon and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1, which each score 53. Only Anthropic's flagship Claude Opus 5.5 scores higher among these models, at 58.

key_facts.fact: Neither Wonder model has downloadable weights, a break from Meta's Llama open-model history; Wonder Full is offered on Muse Code's $50/month Power Usage and $200/month Maximum Usage plans.
key_facts.excerpt: Neither Wonder model is being released with publicly downloadable weights... Power Usage: $50 per month... Maximum Usage: $200 per month, providing 80 times the Everyday plan's usage allowance.

key_facts.fact: Meta says Muse Wonder scores higher on the MemoryBench memory benchmark than Fable, Opus or Astra.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the company's testing, Muse Wonder now scores higher on MemoryBench than Fable, Opus or Astra.

stories.headline: Character.AI files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, with Disney bidding $20M for assets

key_facts.fact: Character Technologies (Character.AI) commenced a voluntary Chapter 11 case in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware to sell all or substantially all of its assets, and plans to keep operating its platform during the sale.
key_facts.excerpt: today announced that it has commenced a voluntary Chapter 11 case in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware... to facilitate a value-maximizing sale of all or substantially all of its assets... The Company intends to continue operating its platform

key_facts.fact: Disney is the stalking horse bidder, paying $20 million for a non-exclusive perpetual license of certain Character.AI intellectual property and claims, plus transition services using former Character.AI employees it hired.
key_facts.excerpt: Disney will serve as stalking horse bidder for a non-exclusive perpetual license of certain Company intellectual property and certain Company claims, in exchange for $20 million and Disney's provision of transition services using former Company employees it has hired.

key_facts.fact: The filing listed estimated liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.
key_facts.excerpt: In its bankruptcy filing, Character listed estimated liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.

key_facts.fact: Disney hired Character.AI's former CEO Karandeep Anand as its CTO last month; the docket shows Google is the largest creditor, owed more than $4 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Disney hired Character.ai's former CEO Karandeep Anand last month to become its CTO... The docket shows that its largest creditor is Google, which the company owed more than $4 million.

key_facts.fact: The company expects the sale process to close in late November or early December 2026, and the Disney bid is subject to higher offers.
key_facts.excerpt: the Company anticipates that the completion of the Sale Process and the closing of any resulting transactions will occur in late November or early December 2026.

key_facts.fact: Character.AI faced lawsuits and safety scrutiny over its chatbots before the filing; Law360 reports it said it was sunk by high development costs.
key_facts.excerpt: saying it was sunk by high development costs and plans an asset auction with a baseline $20 million bid from Disney

stories.headline: Anthropic: small AI models may be months from self-replicating across IoT devices

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team (researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman) published research on October 12 concluding small AI models may be months away from being able to self-replicate on commercial IoT devices such as smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes.
key_facts.excerpt: Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial IoT devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes.

key_facts.fact: In a demo, the team ran Google's Gemma4-26B-A4B across 15 off-brand Android TV boxes (about $55 each, 4GB RAM), producing 0.39 tokens per second.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman ran Gemma4-26B-A4B across the 15 boxes, each with 4GB of RAM... The fleet produced 0.39 tokens per second.

key_facts.fact: Of the open-weight models tested, only Z.ai's GLM-5.2 completed end-to-end replication, reaching all 8 nodes in 4 of 5 trials; a 9B model got inference running on 8 of 9 hardware types.
key_facts.excerpt: Only GLM-5.2 out of our set of tested open-weight models is capable of full end-to-end replication... it spread to 8/8 nodes in 4 out of 5 trials and 7/8 in 1... a 9B model got inference running on 8 of the 9 hardware types we tested.

key_facts.fact: Extrapolating a trend of 13.7 Epoch Capabilities Index points per year for open models of 30B parameters or fewer, Anthropic projects a small model will reach GLM-5.2's level by the end of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: with a gain of 13.7 ECI per year (R 2 of 0.95). If we take GLM-5.2 as a capabilities floor for replication, the trend line puts a small model at that level by the end of 2026.

key_facts.fact: A fleet the size of the Kimwolf botnet (2M+ devices) could host about 133,000 copies of Gemma4-26B-A4B serving roughly 80,000 tokens/s, equivalent to at most about 40 Nvidia H100s; replication would take days per copy.
key_facts.excerpt: we would have ~133k copies... yielding 80k tokens/s across the botnet... our swarm would have at most about 40 H100s-worth of inference... the agents are slow replicators (over 1-2 days per 9B replication).

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said such a replicator would be challenging to shut down because there is no centralized point to shut off, and acknowledged no fully rogue replicator exists yet.
key_facts.excerpt: The AI model would be "challenging to shut down," Anthropic said in a blog post, "since there's no centralized point to shut off." The company acknowledged that there is not yet a "fully rogue replicator."

stories.headline: Anthropic says new defenses cut reasoning harvested by distillers by 90% to 99%

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said on October 12 that new methods have reduced the amount of data harvested from Claude by distillation attackers by around 90 to 99%.
key_facts.excerpt: Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99%.

key_facts.fact: With Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic introduced 'preserved thinking', which prevents API accounts created on or after August 31, 2026 from editing Claude's prior context.
key_facts.excerpt: With Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5, we introduced preserved thinking, a measure that prevents new API accounts (those created on or after August 31, 2026) from editing Claude's prior context.

key_facts.fact: A two-stage classifier with a false positive rate below 0.1% detects extraction attempts; Anthropic has banned tens of thousands of distillation-linked accounts, often within two hours of a campaign starting.
key_facts.excerpt: our safeguards ... false positive rate of less than 0.1%... We've used these defenses to ban tens of thousands of accounts associated with distillation, often in less than two hours after such an account begins a distillation campaign.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says it turned away meaningful revenue and trillions of tokens' worth of paying traffic from distillers.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic says it has turned away meaningful revenue and trillions of tokens of paying traffic from distillers.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's data shows reasoning transcripts give distillers large uplift: a model trained on full Opus 4.8 transcripts scored 80.4% on SWE-bench Verified versus 71.8% when trained on summarized ones.
key_facts.excerpt: a model trained on full transcripts from Opus 4.8 scored 80.4% on SWE-bench Verified, while the same model trained on summarized ones reached 71.8%.

stories.headline: TypeSafe AI, maker of non-text model Jev, raises $870M at $7.5B valuation

key_facts.fact: TypeSafe AI raised $870 million at a $7.5 billion valuation on October 9, 2026, in a round led by Andreessen Horowitz with Sequoia Capital, DCVC and unnamed angels.
key_facts.excerpt: TypeSafe Inc., the creator of the Jev artificial intelligence model, today announced that it has raised $870 million in funding at a $7.5 billion valuation. Andreessen Horowitz led the round with contributions from Sequoia Capital, DCVC and unnamed angel investors.

key_facts.fact: TypeSafe exited stealth on September 15, 2026 with a $40M seed led by DCVC at roughly a $200M valuation, about a 37x step-up in under a month.
key_facts.excerpt: TypeSafe exited stealth on 15 September 2026 with Jev and a $40 million seed led by DCVC at roughly a $200 million valuation; the Series A closed on 9 October at $7.5 billion, a step-up of about 37 times in under a month

key_facts.fact: Jev returns decisions to code as typed values instead of text; a16z says it costs roughly 1/100 to 1/500 of frontier models and is 100x faster on classification at comparable accuracy, reaching 1 trillion tokens in 3 days after launch.
key_facts.excerpt: Jev hands the decision directly to your code as a typed value... Jev is roughly 1/100 to 1/500 the cost of frontier models while being 100x faster for classification tasks at the comparable accuracy... reaching 1 trillion tokens generated in merely 3 days post launch.

key_facts.fact: Jev is already used by about a third of the Fortune 500, according to the company; proceeds will fund more models in the 'System One' series and enterprise features.
key_facts.excerpt: It has already been adopted by about a third of the Fortune 500... Jev is part of a planned model series dubbed System One. TypeSafe will use the proceeds from its funding round to make more additions to the lineup.

key_facts.fact: CEO and co-founder Diogo Almeida is a former OpenAI researcher; a16z general partner Martin Casado joins the board.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2024 by CEO Diogo Almeida, a former OpenAI researcher... Martin Casado, a general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, joins the board.

stories.headline: SpaceXSI bundles Grok, Cursor and X Premium into one 'X Subscription'

key_facts.fact: SpaceXSI introduced The X Subscription on October 12, combining Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium in one plan, rolling out globally over the following days.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're introducing The X Subscription, which brings together Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor, and X Premium in one plan. Over the next few days, we'll make it available to everyone globally.

key_facts.fact: Plans: Free, Plus $8/month, Premium $30/month, Super $100/month and Ultra $200/month; Premium includes SuperGrok, Cursor Pro and X Premium+ benefits previously costing $90/month combined.
key_facts.excerpt: Plus | $8/month... Premium | $30/month | The benefits of SuperGrok, Cursor Pro, and X Premium+, previously $90/month combined... Super | $100/month... Ultra | $200/month

key_facts.fact: Grok and Cursor share one weekly usage pool; third-party models such as Claude or GPT in Cursor are not included and are billed at API list prices from first use.
key_facts.excerpt: Grok and Cursor usage draw from the same included pool... third-party models in Cursor, like Claude or GPT, aren't included in your plan. You can still use them in Cursor, billed at API list prices from the first use

key_facts.fact: Each X Subscription plan includes at least twice as much coding usage with SpaceXSI's own models as the comparable Cursor plan; existing subscribers can keep their plans.
key_facts.excerpt: Each X Subscription plan includes at least twice as much coding usage with our models as the comparable Cursor plan... Nothing changes for existing SuperGrok, Cursor, or X Premium subscribers.

key_facts.fact: SpaceXSI, formerly SpaceXAI, acquired coding startup Cursor in August.
key_facts.excerpt: The company was formerly known as SpaceXAI... the company acquired coding startup Cursor back in August.

stories.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI sought control over what outside AI evaluators publish, Reuters says

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported on October 13 that Anthropic and OpenAI have sought significant control over what outside evaluators can publish, concerned findings could reveal trade secrets, citing two people familiar with the discussions.
key_facts.excerpt: NEW YORK, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Anthropic and OpenAI have sought significant control over what outside evaluators can publish, concerned that findings could reveal trade secrets, according to two people familiar with the discussions.

key_facts.fact: Last month Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said external evaluators should be able to publish key findings 'without editorial control', and OpenAI agreed days later; yet as recently as October 5 both labs sought strict editorial control.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said last month that external evaluators should have the right to publish key findings "without editorial control." OpenAI agreed days later... as recently as October 5, Anthropic and OpenAI were seeking strict editorial control

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said reviewers it has worked with control their methods, conclusions and publications, but it reserves the right to comment on and approve reports from new evaluator firms.
key_facts.excerpt: For new evaluator firms, Anthropic said it reserved the right to comment on and approve reports as the reviewers learn how its models operate and establish a working relationship.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it is not seeking approval rights over full reports; its standard practice is to redact confidential information, and evaluators can disclose whether major redactions were made.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI, for its part, said it was not seeking approval rights over the full text of reports produced by evaluators. It said its standard practice is to redact confidential information

key_facts.fact: Independent evaluation is one of four safety measures in an accord signed by President Trump and AI executives in late September, which has no formal enforcement mechanism; Anthropic named Faculty, Accenture's AI business, as its first embedded evaluator.
key_facts.excerpt: Independent evaluation is one of four safety measures in ... on Super Intelligence, signed by President Donald Trump and leading AI executives in late September... The accord ... has no formal enforcement mechanism.

key_facts.fact: Ideas under discussion include lab staff monitoring embedded review teams and barring reviewers from working at two labs at once.
key_facts.excerpt: Ideas under discussion include having lab staff watch the teams and banning reviewers from working at two labs at once.
